ingredients.description: Acetylated form of lanolin. More comedogenic than regular lanolin due to modification.
Acetylated derivative of lanolin alcohol. More comedogenic than regular lanolin. One of the worst offenders in the lanolin family.
Seaweed-derived extract with very high comedogenic potential. Rich in iodine which can trigger breakouts. Used as thickener and conditioner.
Non-comedogenic soothing agent derived from comfrey. Promotes skin healing and cell regeneration. Safe for all skin types.
Non-comedogenic soothing agent with anti-inflammatory and hydrating properties.
Synthetic polymer thickener and emulsion stabilizer. Creates lightweight gel textures. Not known to be comedogenic.
Light plant oil with low comedogenic potential. Similar to almond oil. Good for sensitive skin.
Non-comedogenic water. Universal solvent and hydrator. Base ingredient in most skincare formulations.
Non-comedogenic oil rich in vitamin E and fatty acids. Well-tolerated by most skin types.
Fat-soluble form of vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Low comedogenic potential but can be problematic for very acne-prone skin.
Rich plant oil with low to moderate comedogenic potential. High in oleic acid. Rating varies by source (2-3).
Non-comedogenic dicarboxylic acid. Excellent for acne and rosacea. Antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. Safe for all skin types.
Natural wax with low comedogenic potential. Rating varies by source (0-2). Generally safe but can be occlusive. Used as thickener and emollient.
Non-comedogenic conditioning agent and emulsifier. Quaternary ammonium compound. Provides slip and detangling in hair and skin products.
Non-comedogenic polysaccharide with soothing and antioxidant properties. Derived from oats or yeast. Excellent for sensitive skin.
Non-comedogenic soothing agent from chamomile. Anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. Excellent for sensitive and irritated skin.
Fatty acid ester with moderate comedogenic potential.
Very low comedogenic humectant and solvent. Gentler alternative to propylene glycol. Safe for most skin types.
Synthetic film-forming polymer used to create breathable, flexible films on skin. Common in sunscreens and long-wear makeup. Not comedogenic.
Non-comedogenic polymer thickener. Creates gel textures. Neutralized with bases like triethanolamine or sodium hydroxide.
Seaweed-derived thickener with very high comedogenic potential. Can be problematic for acne-prone skin. Used in food and cosmetics.
Plant-derived polysaccharide used as thickener. Very low comedogenic risk.
Non-comedogenic plant extract with powerful soothing and healing properties. Rich in asiaticoside and madecassoside. Popular in K-beauty (cica).
Non-comedogenic skin-identical lipid. Essential component of skin barrier. Helps repair damaged barrier and retain moisture. Safe for all skin types.
Non-comedogenic skin-identical lipid. Essential component of skin barrier. Helps repair damaged barrier. Safe for all skin types.
Non-comedogenic skin-identical lipid. Essential component of skin barrier. The 'EOP' stands for Esterified Omega-hydroxy Phytosphingosine. Helps repair damaged barrier.
Mixture of cetyl and stearyl alcohols. Low comedogenic potential. Generally well-tolerated.
Fatty acid ester with high comedogenic potential. Synthetic alternative to spermaceti wax.
Fatty alcohol with low comedogenic potential. Commonly used as thickener and emollient.
Non-comedogenic skin-identical lipid. Essential component of skin barrier. Often combined with ceramides and fatty acids for barrier repair.
Rich plant butter with high comedogenic potential. Very occlusive and can trap sebum in pores.
Popular natural oil with high comedogenic potential due to high lauric acid content. Very occlusive.
Plant oil with moderate comedogenic potential. High in linoleic acid but still moderately comedogenic.
Oil from cotton seeds with moderate comedogenic potential. Contains gossypol.
Fatty acid ester with moderate comedogenic potential.
Low comedogenic silicone that provides slip and occlusion without heaviness. Generally well-tolerated.
Non-comedogenic pH adjuster and buffer. Used to maintain optimal pH in formulations. Safe for all skin types.
Non-comedogenic chelating agent. Binds metal ions to improve preservative efficacy and product stability. Common in cosmetics.
UVB sunscreen agent (phenylbenzimidazole sulfonic acid). Water-soluble, non-comedogenic.
Photostabilizer for avobenzone. Very low comedogenic risk.
Common emollient ester with high comedogenic potential. Often used as silicone alternative.
Non-comedogenic preservative booster and skin conditioner. Often used with phenoxyethanol. Improves skin feel.
Oil from evening primrose seeds with moderate comedogenic potential. Contains GLA (gamma-linolenic acid).
Non-comedogenic humectant that draws moisture to the skin. Safe for all skin types.
Non-comedogenic emulsifier and thickener. Combines glycerin and stearic acid. Self-emulsifying grades exist. Safe for all skin types.
Soybean oil with moderate comedogenic potential. Contains omega-6 fatty acids.
Non-comedogenic alpha hydroxy acid. Smallest AHA molecule, penetrates deeply. Excellent for anti-ageing and pore clearing. Can be irritating at high concentrations.
Light, non-comedogenic oil rich in linoleic acid. Good for oily and acne-prone skin.
Non-comedogenic antioxidant with anti-inflammatory and sebum-regulating properties.
Non-comedogenic oil with ideal omega-6 to omega-3 ratio. Balances oil production and reduces inflammation.
Hydrogenated vegetable oils with moderate comedogenic potential. Occlusive.
Antioxidant and preservative booster. Synergizes with other preservatives to reduce microbial growth. Not comedogenic.
Synthetic polymer thickener and texture enhancer. Creates smooth, non-tacky gels. Not known to be comedogenic.
Branched-chain fatty acid ester with high comedogenic potential.
Highly comedogenic emollient ester. Part of the problematic isopropyl ester series.
Lanolin derivative with moderate comedogenic potential. Part of the isopropyl ester family.
Highly comedogenic emollient ester with unsaturated fatty acid.
Highly comedogenic emollient and penetration enhancer. One of the most tested positive controls in comedogenicity assays.
Part of the problematic isopropyl ester series. Highly comedogenic emollient.
Branched-chain fatty acid ester with high comedogenic potential. Used as emollient in cosmetics.
Liquid wax ester chemically similar to human sebum. Non-comedogenic and well-tolerated by most skin types.
Non-comedogenic alpha hydroxy acid. Gentler than glycolic acid. Also acts as humectant. Good for sensitive skin.
Ethoxylated lanolin alcohol with low comedogenic potential. Safer than lower ethoxylated versions.
Ethoxylated lauryl alcohol with high comedogenic potential. Used as emulsifier and surfactant.
Saturated fatty acid found in coconut oil and palm kernel oil. Has antimicrobial properties but is highly comedogenic.
Oil from flax seeds with high comedogenic potential. Rich in omega-3 fatty acids but problematic for pores.
Non-comedogenic alpha hydroxy acid. Larger molecule than glycolic acid, gentler on skin. Good for sensitive and acne-prone skin.
UVA sunscreen agent (menthyl anthranilate). Non-comedogenic.
Non-comedogenic mineral oil. Cosmetic-grade only. Excellent occlusive. Often wrongly feared due to confusion with industrial-grade mineral oil. Safe for all skin types.
Saturated fatty acid found in nutmeg and coconut oil. Moderately comedogenic.
Fatty acid ester with high comedogenic potential. Used as emollient and conditioning agent.
Waxy emollient ester with very high comedogenic potential.
Non-comedogenic form of vitamin B3. Regulates sebum, reduces inflammation, and minimizes pores.
Monounsaturated omega-9 fatty acid. Moderately comedogenic and can disrupt skin barrier at high concentrations.
Ethoxylated oleyl alcohol emulsifier with high comedogenic rating.
Ethoxylated oleyl alcohol with high comedogenic potential.
Unsaturated fatty alcohol derived from oleic acid. Highly comedogenic.
Plant oil with low to moderate comedogenic potential. Rich in oleic acid. Rating varies by refinement level. Extra virgin has higher rating than refined.
Natural wax from rice bran. Very low comedogenic risk, possible mild congestion for very oily skin.
UVB sunscreen agent (octyl dimethyl PABA). Non-comedogenic.
Saturated fatty acid found in palm oil and animal fats. Low to moderate comedogenic potential.
Non-comedogenic form of vitamin B5. Humectant and soothing agent. Promotes wound healing and skin barrier repair. Safe for all skin types.
Plant oil with low comedogenic potential. Rich in fatty acids. Caution for those with nut allergies.
Ethoxylated lanolin with high comedogenic potential. Part of the problematic lanolin derivative family.
Non-comedogenic emulsifier. High ethoxylation (40) makes it safe. Used to blend oil and water phases. Different from lower PEG stearates.
Non-comedogenic peptide that stimulates collagen production. Cell-communicating ingredient. Safe for all skin types including acne-prone.
Non-comedogenic occlusive. Rating 0. Used in wound care and eczema treatment. Excellent barrier repair. Often wrongly feared.
Non-comedogenic preservative. Broad-spectrum antimicrobial. One of the most common preservatives in cosmetics. Safe at typical concentrations (<1%).
Non-comedogenic skin-identical lipid. Precursor to ceramides. Has antimicrobial properties. Safe for all skin types.
Dispersing agent for mineral pigments. Very low comedogenic risk.
Non-comedogenic surfactant and solubilizer. Used to dissolve oils into water-based products. Low ethoxylation (20) is safe.
Non-comedogenic pH adjuster and buffer. Used to maintain optimal pH in formulations. Safe for all skin types.
Non-comedogenic humectant and solvent. Penetration enhancer that helps other ingredients absorb. Safe for most skin types but can be irritating at high concentrations.
Non-comedogenic vitamin A derivative. Gold standard for anti-ageing and acne treatment. Can cause irritation during adjustment period (retinization).
Low comedogenic oil rich in vitamin A and essential fatty acids. Good for most skin types.
Non-comedogenic oil very high in linoleic acid. Excellent for acne-prone skin.
Non-comedogenic beta hydroxy acid that exfoliates inside pores. Excellent for acne-prone and oily skin.
Plant oil with low comedogenic potential. Rich in sesamin and sesamolin. Used in traditional medicine.
Non-comedogenic plant butter rich in fatty acids and vitamins. Excellent emollient with anti-inflammatory properties.
Salt form of hyaluronic acid. Non-comedogenic humectant with excellent water-binding capacity. Different molecular weights penetrate different skin layers.
Non-comedogenic mild surfactant and emulsifier. Derived from lactic acid and lauric acid. Gentle cleansing agent.
Non-comedogenic natural moisturizing factor. Excellent humectant. Part of skin's natural moisture barrier. Safe for all skin types.
Emulsifier derived from sorbitol and isostearic acid. Very low comedogenic risk.
Emulsifier derived from sorbitol and oleic acid. Moderately comedogenic.
Hydrogenated, stable form of squalene. Non-comedogenic and excellent emollient. Safe for all skin types.
Natural component of human sebum. Highly unstable and oxidizes easily, which can lead to comedogenic effects. DIFFERENT from squalane (hydrogenated, stable version).
Ethoxylated stearyl alcohol emulsifier with high comedogenic rating.
Non-ionic emulsifier with lower ethoxylation than Steareth-20. Mild comedogenic potential at high concentrations.
Non-ionic emulsifier derived from stearyl alcohol. Mild comedogenic potential at high concentrations.
Saturated fatty acid commonly used as emulsifier and thickener. Low to moderate comedogenic potential.
Fatty alcohol with low comedogenic potential. Used as thickener and emollient.
Fatty acid ester with high comedogenic potential. Used as emollient in cosmetic formulations.
Mineral with moderate comedogenic rating but excellent anti-acne properties. Keratolytic agent that helps unclog pores. Used in acne treatments.
Non-comedogenic oil rich in linoleic acid. Light and well-tolerated.
Light plant oil with low comedogenic potential. Rich in vitamin E and fatty acids. Generally well-tolerated.
Non-comedogenic essential oil with antimicrobial properties. Effective against acne-causing bacteria.
Non-comedogenic mineral sunscreen and pigment. Safe for all skin types.
Non-comedogenic vitamin E derivative. More stable than pure tocopherol. Antioxidant and skin conditioning properties. Converts to active vitamin E on skin.
pH adjuster and emulsifier with low comedogenic potential. Can be irritating to sensitive skin.
Silane coupling agent for mineral sunscreens. Very low comedogenic risk.
Ester of citric acid used as a fragrance fixative, solvent, and deodorant agent. Biodegradable and non-comedogenic.
Chelating agent that binds metal ions to improve formula stability. Biodegradable alternative to EDTA. Not comedogenic.
Non-comedogenic natural moisturizing factor (NMF). Humectant and mild exfoliant. At concentrations above 10%, acts as keratolytic. Safe for all skin types.
Non-comedogenic pure vitamin C. Potent antioxidant. Brightens skin and stimulates collagen. Unstable, requires proper formulation. Can be irritating at high concentrations.
Non-comedogenic vitamin E. Potent antioxidant. Protects skin from oxidative stress. Stable and well-tolerated. Note: Tocopheryl acetate (ester form) may be comedogenic for some.
Highly comedogenic oil rich in vitamin E but problematic for acne-prone skin.
Non-comedogenic polysaccharide thickener. Fermented from corn sugar. Used to stabilize emulsions and add texture.
Non-comedogenic mineral sunscreen agent with soothing and antimicrobial properties.

synonyms.synonym: hydroxyethyl acrylate sodium acryloyldimethyl taurate copolymer
